content.text: Uncertainty is the birthplace of possibility.
content.context: Written at 3am during a Bridge pivot. The not-knowing felt like a full stop — until I realized it was just the line break before the next stanza.

content.text: Everything you are is built from everything you're not.
content.context: A caption I've returned to more times than I've posted. Identity as negative space — the shape defined by what doesn't fit.

content.text: Every venture is a verse — the pitch a volta, the pivot iambic.
content.context: The thesis behind Business Is Poetry. Not a metaphor. A methodology. When you treat a startup like a poem — with meter, tension, and resolution — you stop guessing and start composing.

content.text: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
content.context: The compass I return to when systems break or plans collapse. The only variable I actually control is my response.

content.text: Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens.
content.context: The Stoic frame for building startups: control your inputs obsessively, hold your outcomes lightly.

content.text: Out beyond ideas of wrongdoing and rightdoing, there is a field. I'll meet you there.
content.context: The creative space I try to operate from — before judgment, before categories. Where the real conversations happen.
The most useful poem I know. Not about death — about intensity. About not sleepwalking through your one window of influence.

content.text:
I'm Nobody! Who are you?
Are you — Nobody — too?
content.context: The anti-personal-brand manifesto. Two lines that do more than any LinkedIn bio.

content.text: It's not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters.
content.context: Posted this the morning after our first major Bridge rejection. Still holds.

content.text: The best pitches aren't persuasion — they're permission. You're giving someone language to believe something they already feel.
content.context: A note I wrote after watching three different founders pitch the same product. The winner didn't have better features. He had better permission-giving.

content.text: Clarity is a product of elimination, not addition.
content.context: About writing, about design, about building. The same principle across all three: you reach clarity by cutting, not accumulating.

content.text: What happens when you treat a venture not as a machine to optimize, but as a poem to compose — with volta, meter, and deliberate silence?
content.context: Business Is Poetry: On Building Like a Poet — the essay that started everything on this site.
